correctness.rationale: For each normalized primitive Dirichlet angle a/q, exact path eigenmodes exist on the arms with q dividing n_i=L_i+1; the central eigen-equation is a nonzero single linear functional and gives nullity (r_q-1)_+. Summing over phi(q) primitive fractions reconstructs the entire zero-hub eigenbasis. The orthogonal hyperplane projector has arm diagonal 1-(1/n_i)/W_q; sine-square summation gives the stated Ramanujan formula. Each term is nonnegative, so zero-site survival iff every shared denominator divides s, equivalently lcm of gcds h_i divides s; global extinction iff pairwise coprime n_i. The dissipative complement has strictly negative eigenvalue imaginary parts since any real eigenvector would be dark, so finite-dimensional Jordan evolution decays exponentially. Independently constructed adjacency matrices and spectral projectors for five heterogeneous/homogeneous spider tuples matched all local weights and the dark dimension.
residual_risks: Numerical spectral tests are not an infinite proof and may have tolerance effects; infinite result rests on reconstructed Dirichlet modes and dissipativity.
